title: Spaceflight is associated with mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation suppression and immune dysregulation that persist after return: a cross-mission transcriptomic analysis
content:
Abstract
Human spaceflight exposes astronauts to microgravity and space radiation, yet whether these stressors produce a common molecular response across tissues has remained unclear. To address this, we performed a cross-mission meta-analysis of 70 spaceflight-versus-ground-control transcriptomic comparisons spanning 21 tissues and 16 missions from the NASA Open Science Data Repository, stratified by cumulative radiation exposure. We found that mitochondrial dysfunction is a consistent transcriptional signature of spaceflight: oxidative phosphorylation was significantly downregulated in the vast majority of in-flight datasets with exposure ≥10.34 mGy, accompanied by coordinated suppression of mitochondrial and cytosolic translation and mitochondrial protein import. In-flight datasets also showed activation of HIF-1α target genes and broad innate and adaptive immune dysregulation, including upregulation of mitochondrial DNA- and RNA-sensing transcripts consistent with mtDAMP-driven inflammation. After return to Earth, HIF-associated and most immune responses resolved, whereas oxidative phosphorylation suppression persisted in high-exposure datasets, dissociating transient adaptive responses from a sustained mitochondrial lesion. Mitochondrial suppression scaled with cumulative exposure and was greater in older, male, and C57BL/6 mice. Together, these findings establish mitochondrial dysfunction as a consistent, exposure-dependent, and persistent transcriptional feature to spaceflight, identifying mitochondrial bioenergetics and protein homeostasis as priority countermeasure targets for long-duration lunar and Mars missions.
Biological insight
We identify mitochondrial dysfunction as a conserved molecular response to spaceflight, characterized by suppression of oxidative phosphorylation, altered mitochondrial and cytosolic translation, and disruption of mitochondrial protein homeostasis. Technological innovation: We developed an integrated transcriptomic framework that harmonizes independent spaceflight datasets across missions, tissues, and biological backgrounds while preserving dataset-specific experimental structure. Benefit of integration: Joint analysis of 70 comparisons spanning 21 tissues and 16 missions revealed exposure-dependent and persistent mitochondrial alterations that were not apparent from individual datasets, while distinguishing sustained oxidative phosphorylation suppression from more transient stress and immune responses. This integrative approach provides a systems-level framework for identifying conserved biological responses and prioritizing mitochondrial pathways as potential targets for spaceflight countermeasures.
